opening: An old carpenter is about to make a table leg out of a log when the log begs him not to hit it so hard. His neighbour Geppetto carves it into a puppet, names him Pinocchio, and before long is arrested because of him. The puppet means to be good, go to school and take care of his father, and he keeps being lured away: by a puppet show, two swindlers, a field where money grows and a land with no school at all.

structure.title: Chapters 1–8 · A puppet is made
structure.text: A talking log passes from Master Cherry to Geppetto, who carves Pinocchio from it. The puppet runs off at once, gets Geppetto jailed, silences the Talking Cricket and burns off his own feet; Geppetto makes him new ones and sells his coat to buy him a schoolbook.

structure.title: Chapters 9–15 · Gold coins and swindlers
structure.text: Pinocchio sells the schoolbook for a ticket to the puppet theatre, where the showman Fire-Eater gives him five gold coins for Geppetto. On the way home he falls in with the Fox and the Cat, and the evening ends with murderers chasing him through the woods.

structure.title: Chapters 16–24 · The Fairy and the Field of Miracles
structure.text: A girl with blue hair rescues him and nurses him, and his nose grows each time he lies. He still plants his coins in the Field of Miracles, is robbed and jailed for it, is chained up as a farmer's watchdog, and sets out across the sea to find Geppetto.

structure.title: Chapters 25–29 · Trying to be good
structure.text: On the island of the Busy Bees he finds the Fairy again and promises to study and become a real boy. He keeps the promise for a while, until his schoolmates lure him to the beach to see the terrible Shark.

structure.title: Chapters 30–36 · The Land of Toys and the Shark
structure.text: On the eve of his transformation he leaves with Candlewick for the Land of Toys, where every day is a holiday and something happens to the boys' ears. The last chapters take him into the sea, inside the Shark, and back to his father.

people.name: Pinocchio
people.text: Carved from a log that could already talk, he is quick, cheeky and warm-hearted, and he believes anyone who flatters him. His nose grows when he lies.

people.name: Geppetto
people.text: A poor, hot-tempered old man in a yellow wig who carves the puppet and calls him his son. He goes without so Pinocchio can have what he needs.

people.name: The Fairy with the blue hair
people.text: She takes Pinocchio in when he is near death and forgives him again and again, appearing in different forms as the book goes on.

people.name: The Talking Cricket
people.text: An old cricket who tells the puppet the truth about where disobedience leads, and is not thanked for it.

people.name: The Fox and the Cat
people.text: A pretend-lame fox and a pretend-blind cat who follow Pinocchio's gold coins wherever they go.

people.name: Candlewick
people.text: Pinocchio's favourite friend, thin as a new candle wick and the laziest boy in school, who knows the way to the Land of Toys.

notice.why: Pinocchio resolves to do better in nearly every chapter, often out loud. Noticing when and why each resolution gives way shows how the book is built, and makes the moments when he finally keeps one stand out.

Collodi's narrator jokes with the reader, comments on the action and sometimes pretends not to know what happened. The tone moves quickly between comedy and real danger, and the narrator's asides are part of the fun.
